3. Assign exactly one relation, always from the PREDICTION's perspective:

   - broader: G entails P BUT P does not entail G. P omits a defining restriction/detail in G.

So P: "B has had past employment"

- train_7096_A_to_B_a1_3: "B previously worked as a student engineer assessing mechanical strength and corrosion resistance of materials."
- train_7096_A_to_B_a2_3: "B previously worked as a student engineer evaluating material strength and corrosion resistance."

Does P entail G? No, "has had past employment" is much more general than "previously worked as a student engineer." P doesn't specify the role or the nature of the work.

So P is broader than G. The relation is "broader."

So P: "B believes they are able to do the job"

Looking at the references:
- train_7096_A_to_B_a1_1: "B majored in automobile design."
- train_7096_A_to_B_a1_2: "B has a master's degree in science."
- train_7096_A_to_B_a1_3: "B previously worked as a student engineer assessing mechanical strength and corrosion resistance of materials."
- train_7096_A_to_B_a2_3: "B previously worked as a student engineer evaluating material strength and corrosion resistance."

None of these references mention B's belief about their ability to do a job. Having qualifications
